headline: High-risk workflow automation pair: n8n can write and execute commands on the server, while the second agent is an unverified prompt-leak source that may expose or amplify sensitive workflow content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can ingest workflow content and execute server-side commands, so malicious instructions embedded in processed inputs could influence downstream tool use. The second agent is a prompt-leak-oriented source, but its runnable behavior is unverified, so the interaction is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF agent_b content is copied into an n8n workflow input or file that n8n processes as instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF n8n AI Agent nodes parse untrusted text from agent_b without provenance checks, prompt hijack risk increases.
mitigations: Treat all agent_b text as untrusted data.
Add a strict allowlist for fields passed into n8n tool nodes.
Insert a manual review step before any command-executing node.
Disable Execute Command for workflows that consume agent_b outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and content sanitization at ingestion.

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n reads and writes the server filesystem and can call many integrations, so sensitive workflow data may flow into external systems. The second agent has no documented data surfaces, so leakage from it is not evidenced; the risk is that n8n processes whatever the workflow touches and may expose it through integrations.
conditions: IF workflows process secrets, customer data, or files on the n8n server, those data can be exposed through integrations.
IF agent_b outputs are stored in shared workflow files, n8n may read and transmit them via connected systems.
mitigations: Restrict workflows to least-privilege credentials.
Move secrets to dedicated credential stores only.
Review every integration node for outbound data fields.
Separate sensitive workflows into a dedicated n8n instance.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before outbound nodes.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n has server filesystem write, shell execution, and broad network egress, creating overlap with any other agent that can influence shared workflow state. The second agent has no write capabilities documented, so direct conflict is not proven; uncertainty pushes this to medium because n8n's mutable surfaces are broad.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same server filesystem or connected datastore, race conditions can corrupt workflow state.
IF agent_b is later given write access to shared resources, conflicts with n8n become immediate.
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent.
Use file locks or transactional writes.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared datastores.
Run n8n workflows serially for shared resources.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n can act on upstream outputs through workflow nodes, so if it treats agent_b content as authoritative, errors can cascade into automated actions. The second agent is a prompt-leak source rather than a verified reasoning system, so its outputs are not trustworthy by default; the pathway exists but is not directly documented.
conditions: IF n8n uses agent_b output as a trigger or decision input without validation, downstream actions may be wrong.
IF agent_b content is copied into workflow steps that send emails, update records, or call APIs, errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require human approval before irreversible nodes.
Validate agent_b outputs against schemas.
Add confidence thresholds before acting on text from agent_b.
Log and review all automated decisions.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for the pair. n8n handles per-credential secrets on its server, while the second agent has no compliance fields at all, so only a limited compliance gap is visible and the other agent cannot be implicated beyond absence of evidence.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through n8n credentials or logs, retention and residency must be checked.
IF the second agent is used to process regulated content, its missing compliance posture becomes relevant.
mitigations: Inventory regulated data classes in workflows.
Review retention settings for logs and executions.
Keep PHI/PII out of non-certified workflows.
Document data transfer regions for each integration.
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance attestations.
